utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know any of the people on these photographs? These photographs have dates: April, June, other months in 1992.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one seems familiar to me, as far as I manage to see on these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Madam, could you please tell me in that year, 1992, and in 1993, in the Bosnian embassy in Zagreb did you come across any individuals of Arab origin who came to get documents needed for entering Bosnia-Herzegovina? I'm asking you about 1992 when you came to the embassy every now and then and the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not come across such people.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any knowledge to the effect that they did receive documents from the embassy in Zagreb for entering Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please look at the pages in this document 0328-4603. That is the first page. These are certain tables. When you find them, tell me, please. And it also says 1, and then you go all the way to table 17.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the page that ends in 4603.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Trial Chamber, I would like to say that the translation was made only for those parts that we are going to refer to -- or rather, that I'm going to refer to in my cross-examination, and we have given the entire text to be translated, so then we are going to put the translation into e-court once we get it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So we see here that this is a document of the ARBiH centre for logistics with Supreme Command headquarters Zagreb Samobor group and it says here the army of -- the Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina centre for logistics of the Supreme Command headquarters Zagreb-Samobor group. Did you know of the existence of this group in Samobor?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you knew Mr. Hasan Cengic and you confirmed that you saw him in 1992 in Zagreb. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Suajba Seta?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you come across him?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came across him at the embassy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In 1992 or later?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. When I came there as attache.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was it that he did then?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: His work and the work done by some other colleagues is what I thought was related to the electronic transfer of documents coming from me and other colleagues to Bosnia and Herzegovina. So that was my knowledge. The transfer of documents from Zagreb to Sarajevo in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note we cannot hear Ms. Nozica because she overlapped.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Suajba Seta. Thank you. We saw a document related to an official appointment from July 1993. I'm just going to ask you about some persons, and I'm referring to number 1, for example, where the salary for 1992 is referred to. Ejub Husika, did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Do you want me to go through this list and then I'll tell you?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kalajdzic Sulejman.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You knew him?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does it say convoy for Visoko next to his name?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are speaking at the same time the interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The interpreters have already many times requested you, Ms. Nozica, and also the witness, that you should slow down and to have one minute at least or something like that in between the questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Madam, you heard this. It pertains to both of us. So we will slow down. Number 5, Silajdzic Sulejman. You knew him. And I would just like to say for the transcript that on the 8th of January, 1993, there was some convoy going to Visoko. Is that what this paper says?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It says -- no. In the document I'm looking at it is the 22nd of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What item are you looking at?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I beg your pardon. Number 5 is the 8th of January. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you would tell us roughly whether you knew anybody else.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Person number 8. And the same person is referred to under number 16, the same person referred as referred to in number 5. And I don't know anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. We have identified some people. So let me put it this way now: Number 5, 9, and 10. Numbers 5, 9, and 10. It says that there are some convoys going to Visoko, to Vlasenica, and yet another convoy going to Visoko under number 10. Did you have any knowledge about this period, that is to say the month of December 1992, 1993, that there were some convoys going in these directions?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time I was in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In the period while you were staying in Croatia did you have any knowledge about some convoys being prepared and some convoys going? You were obviously interested in going back to Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any knowledge. At that time, I was in contact with the UNHCR and I was asking about what the possibilities were in term of humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Madam, table number 2. I just have a brief question. Number 1, 2, 3, 4 says that these are salaries for 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Doesn't this document show that the centre for logistics of the Supreme Command headquarters existed in Zagreb at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document does speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's move on to table number 3, and I'm coming up to something that I consider to be vital as far as your testimony is concerned so far, so let's look at table number 3 now. Under 1 it is Sulejman Kalajdzic. It is a convoy of equipment and materiel for Visoko. Do you know what was in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that there was the main logistics base in Visoko that was called Gloc? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Later on when you returned to Bosnia did you learn that it was the main logistical base for supplying the BH army?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: While you were in Zagreb -- you say you didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us look at numbers 10 and 11. The convoy is going to Visoko once again, and it says the arrival of four trucks, trailer trucks, Saja's trucks. Now, because I haven't got much time I'm going to have to go through this a little more quickly. So let's take a look at table 4. We'll skip table 5 -- or, rather, let -- this is still 1992. We see under number 14 a convoy carrying equipment and materiel. Under 4 it says convoy, and we see the funds set aside. Now, these are considerable funds, as you can see. The document was obtained from the embassy, the Bosnian embassy in Zagreb. Did you have any information at the time or subsequently about the way in which all these activities were financed? And I'm asking you this connection with your answer when you said that you had hardly any resources or negligible resources coming to you from Bosnian to finance the refugees. So did you know how activities of this kind were financed? Did you have the knowledge then or subsequently?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither then nor subsequently, except much later from the mass media.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What did you learn then from the mass media?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That this was financed from sources and funds of assistance that the article in the weekly Dan referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mean the funds that arrived in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the press wrote about and the media broadcast. That's what I knew about. When it was broadcast and made public.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May we now move on to a period when you arrived, and that was March 1993, was it not?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's go through this as quickly as possible and look at the it penultimate page, page 16. That's the one that I want to focus on now. We have here the 22nd of April, 1993, an entry under number 8. We have a convoy with six trailer trucks of equipment to Gorazde. Now, you mentioned a convoy that was held up for a long time because it didn't have the necessary permit. Mr. Karnavas asked you that. And then under number 8 here and again under number 13 here we have materiel and equipment for the 208th mountain brigade of the armed forces of the RBiH and the date is the 22nd of April, the 24th of April twice. Now, based on this document, did you know that weapons and trailer trucks, some going to Gorazde intended for the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina precisely at that time when this trailer truck was not able to move, in fact, was moving to Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then nor later?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I didn't know then, and I didn't know later.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Madam, working in the embassy did you know how weapons were procured, purchased, or, rather, did you know that this logistical centre of the Supreme Command Staff both in Zagreb and in Split during this period of time, which is 1992 and 1993, up until May as we see can from these documents, that these logistical centres were procuring weapons and sending them to Bosnia-Herzegovina, to the BH army? Did you know about that, that they -- that these resources were coming through or from Croatia? From official sources, unofficial sources. You had various conversations. You mentioned Mr. Silajdzic. You met Mr. Hasan Cengic. What do you think his role was in Zagreb, and did you have any information whatsoever about the weapons which were going across Croatia into Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know of the problems that certain individuals were facing, Mr. Asim Karamehmedovic, for instance, Mr. Hasan Cengic. I don't remember the exact period, but they did have problems linked to the procurement and transport of weapons, and I did know that this was linked to Slovenia, had to do with Slovenia and Croatia. My first information came from the media. I learnt very little, almost nothing at all, outside that. I didn't discuss the issues. I didn't try to learn about this from other employees at the embassy either.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: During your testimony, what made an impression on me was the persistence and emotion with which you spoke about the plight of the refugees and said that certain refugees didn't have any money even to use ferries, ferry boats. Now, later on when you learnt, as you say, from the media about all these funds, which in one way or another were in the possession of the embassy in Zagreb, didn't you ask anyone why you were not given part of those funds which could be used to -- which could be used for the refugees to alleviate their plight? Did you talk to anyone after learning all about this, that there were those funds, that there was all that money in Zagreb; whereas, your department had very little resources?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did wonder privately. It occupied me a great deal. I spoke to the former director of the directorate for displaced persons and refugees. Neither of us knew that -- well, we thought that there was no money. And I'm very sorry that if money really did exist, why it wasn't geared towards looking after and helping the refugees and of course displaced persons at the time that I was still in Bosnia, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you discuss this issue with the ambassador? You mentioned the directress, which was Mrs. Sokic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But she was in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I did talk to Mrs. -- I did talk about funds to Mrs. Turkovic, and she clearly told me in no uncertain terms that the embassy had no funds and that the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had no funds, and then I started writing about projects which I submitted to donors whom I considered might finance them and accept them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're going to move on to my last topic. On page 49, line 20 up until page 50, line 9 of yesterday's testimony, that is say, on the 19th of June, you said that you visited Croatian refugees from Kakanj and Zenica at the stadium called Poljud. Now, this was after Ambassador Bisera Turkovic had visited the same location. Is that right? Is that what you said? Do you want me to repeat?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm just waiting for them to finish interpreting. No, that's not right. I said Ambassador Turkovic visited them while they were at the Poljud-Split stadium, and that I visited them at Pinete.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From this, I can conclude that you're talking actually about the same group of refugees; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do believe it was the same group.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the group that you yourself visited in Pinete which is in Istria, is it not, for the record, just to make that clear. That's in northern Croatia, the northern Croatia coast. You said that you learnt that she was at the stadium in Poljud for just a few days, or rather, the group was there and then it was transferred; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed us a document, and would you please look at it now. It is P 05960. P 05960 in the Prosecution binder. When you find it, let me know.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Fine. In response to the Prosecutor's questions, you said that that could have been the group that you talked to in Pinete; right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a report, on the last page, dated the 26th of October, 1993, and I'd like to ask you to look at the second paragraph on page 1, to see how the group arrived at Pinete. You can read it out. It says that the group set off from Metkovici across Ploce in ships and arrived in Pula, a group numbering 1.500 displaced persons. You'll find that in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, then, when I say that Mrs. Turkovic couldn't have visited this group or that you visited a different group, because quite obviously it's not the group that was in Poljud; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, both can't be possible, so can you tell me now? You expressly said that Mrs. Turkovic visited the group at Poljud and that that group was soon transferred to Pinete in Istria, after which you visited it; whereas, here you -- here it says, and you confirm to the Prosecutor, that it was the same group. But quite obviously this group was never at Poljud. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thought it was the same group. I probably made an oversight in the portion of the text which speaks about the group that was transported by ship. It doesn't say that there was a group from Poljud, but I claim that there was the group, as well, from the information media in Croatia who reported on refugees that were at Poljud.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you talked to that group, the group that was at Poljud and which later arrived at Pinete, and they told you that they arrived because allegedly they were afraid of the Mujahedin and that that's how they came to leave their homes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't put the accent on whether it was the same group or not. What I claimed and what I claim today is that I visited a group of Croats from an area and that I talked to them in Pinete, and I conveyed exactly in my report what those refugees informed me about.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the transcript, I'd like to remind you of the transcript of the 19th of June, lines 50, et cetera, that it was a group of refugees visited by Ambassador Turkovic at Poljud and several days later they were transferred to Pinete, and that's when you visited them in Pinete afterwards, later on. So this is quite obviously not the same group. And let's take a look at what group it was that Ambassador Turkovic visited. Look at P 03765 now, please. It's a document that you've already been shown today by my colleague Mr. Karnavas. The number is P 03765.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at page 2 in the English version. Its all on page 1 in English. First of all, the document is dated the 28th of July 1993, let's say that; and then on page 2, it says the following: "In this connection, I wish to mention that immediately upon the refugees' arrival Central Bosnia, I went to Poljud to visit them and issued instructions to ensure resources for them from the logistical centre Split. I organised bread distribution and asked that they be transferred to better accommodation." From this document and from this statement, the ambassador says that in July, she visited those refugees at Poljud; and from what she says, it would emerge that she did what she could for the Croatian refugees, that she asked that bread be distributed to them, and that she invested efforts to provide them with better accommodation. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of what emerges from this, I know that she went to Split, that she was put in contact with the refugees, and that's the same thing that she writes in the letter here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What emerges logically from this, and that's the only thing, is that the refugees visited by Ambassador Turkovic in Poljud and the ones that you confirmed yesterday as having met in Pinete confirming a Prosecution document, that it cannot be the same group of refugees, because these others arrived on the 20th of October, 1993; whereas, Ambassador Turkovic is writing a letter on the 28th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I object. I've been trying to keep my mouth closed this last section today, to not get on my feet, but this is pure fantasy. For the counsel to suggest that because the ambassador visited one set of refugees or displaced persons in July, on one occasion, that that means it's impossible that either this woman or the ambassador could have interviewed or gone to another group of displaced persons at another time in 1993, and that somehow both can't be possibly be true is just outlandish. I mean, it's just absolutely outlandish to say there is an inconsistency between this document and the other documents. Two different times, two different trips that the witness has confirmed and there is no evidence to the contrary, and this is just -- this is not proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but it seems that the Prosecutor is testifying now. The Prosecutor can look at the witness statement, and she spoke of the same event. Now, of course, the witness can say there were two or three groups, but the witness spoke about the same event and that is the reason why I endeavoured to show that this was impossible, that it was the same groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You told us that the refugees told you of the conditions under which they left Kakanj. I'd now like to ask you to tell me the following: Did you make a note of names?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you ask people when you talked to them who they were? Did they introduce themselves? So when you made your notes of your conversations with them, wouldn't it be logical -- well, we saw a series -- or rather, when people complained to you, members, I have to say members of the Bosniak people during individual periods, you had the names. Now, the people you talked to this time, you had no names. Didn't they give you any names? You didn't write them down? They didn't tell it you of the circumstances they left?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did give me this information. They introduced themselves. I knew who I was talking to. I knew their first and last names, and they gave me answers to the questions I was interested in. And, quite literally, I asked them whether they were well taken care of, whether they had accommodation, whether they had a dry and warm place to live, what would happen to their children, would they be able to continue their education. And since they didn't say that they have any burning problem and that they needed essential assistance from the BH embassy, I didn't feel that I had to write a separate report or ask assistance of the UN or other organisations present in Croatia. So that is why there's no separate report about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. That is what, objectively speaking, and we heard what the Prosecutor had to say, is making this mix-up, because you have reports about everything you did, except for this visit to the Croatian refugees. So we can't establish when it happened, when it took place. Now, you said that those refugees told you that they had left because they were told that the Mujahedin were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Where are the reports? I mean, we have reports for everything else she did, and then counsel tries to make an inference of impeachment. And there is just no foundation for that. I'm sorry to be on my feet. I'd really would rather not be on my feet, but it's not proper. It's simply not proper for the counsel to make statements not in the record, not supported evidence, act as if it is evidence, and put to the witness. While you made notes about everything else, there is no evidence of that. There is simply no evidence of that, so she can't put it to the witness in that way. I'm sorry. I really did not want to object, but there really have to be some rules in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, do you have any evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the problem is that the witness has no evidence and no information about the visit to the Croatian refugees because that's what the witness said, and that's the only thing that I said and we're sorry that it didn't exist. And we saw that the Prosecution showed us a series of reports from other meetings, and I just took note of that with regret, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Might I be allowed to add a piece of information? I did compile a report from my official visit to Pinete; and in that report, I did not include the names and surnames of the refugees that I talked to. However, the general observation was made that I visited them and that they were taken care of, that they had recognised refugee status, and that they didn't have any problems and I left. And that is included and contained in my report and the report is in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Madam, I asked you something else. I asked you about the information that you said you had received from refugees about the circumstances under which they left Zenica, Kakanj, et cetera, that apparently they had been told that they would be slaughtered, killed by the Mujahedin. So that is what we are discussing. Did you write down who told you that? Did you include that in your report? Do you have any names?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information is included in my report. These were refugees I contacted in Pinete, and I included this in my report; not the names and surnames of the refugees, but what mattered to me was that every institution should do whatever was necessary and whatever they could on the basis of the information that I provided. These Mujahedin, even if they did exist, could no longer get close to the refugees once they were in Croatia. So it wasn't important for me to give the name and surname of the said individual. That was my logic in terms of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have spent a terrible -- terribly long amount of time on this. I just asked you whether you knew the names and surnames of these persons or whether you included that in your report, and please, that would be the end of that. Now I'm going to conclude, and I'm going to use my last document. We saw from this report of Mrs. Turkovic that she visited Poljud, the refugees there, and she provided whatever was necessary for them. As we look at this report, it seems obvious that the Embassy of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Zagreb took care about the suffering Croats and Muslims. That's what they were called then. Can we put it that way?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we please look at a document? That was the last one, the last digits being 499. It should be the one but last document in the binder.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now whether you refer this. You could remember - you were there at the time - so let's have a look at this. What is all of this about? The Embassy of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Zagreb. Infamous lies at village Doljani near Jablanica became a participant in committed crimes over Croatian civilians. First of all, can I ask you whether you knew about the crime committed in Doljani against Croats?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about that from media in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's read some of the important parts in this document. It says here that "Despite indisputable facts and evidence and despite recognisable pictures of massacred and murdered Croats at the village of Doljani near Jablanica, on television and through the media, this went all round the world. The Embassy of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Zagreb issues a denial and denies that crimes were committed saying the during the occupation of Doljani by Muslim criminal groups of the so-called ARBiH, which participated domestic Muslims from Doljani and Jablanica and Mujahedin, one civilian who entered the area with his herd of sheep accidentally." Ivan Marjanovic is the name of the person signing this document, but let's look at this. It says that this is a denial of the Embassy of the Republic of Croatia and that it was sent to all the media, not only in Croatia but throughout the world, in order to cover up the crime committed. "So far it has been proven that 42 civilians were executed in massacres and also that over 200 Croat civilians were Doljani went missing; and then it says further on that they were put up in a prison in Jablanica, that they were detained there. The Honourable Judges have the translation, but could they please look at the original. You can see here that this denial came from the embassy in Zagreb, and you can even see the telephone number. Is that right? And the date is the 10th of August, 1993. You can see that as well, and the massacre happened on the 27th and 28th of July, 1993. And it says here that this denial indeed, and it is very surprising that a civilian got killed. He got killed accidentally as he was herding his sheep. And this is practically 13 days after the crime was committed when it could have been established beyond any doubt that the crime had been committed in Doljani. Did you know that the embassy expressed its views in this way before and after it had it the possibility of objectively viewing the suffering of Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You did not know about this it press release of the embassy?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You were there then?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was it possible for that many things to be going on at the embassy that you did not know about? How big was this office? How many staff members were there in the embassy? How many permanently employed persons were there at the embassy?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I would prefer explaining the organisation of my own office.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that quite a few things could have been going on at the embassy, quite a few activities without me knowing about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Finally, a question, Ms. Krajsek. You insisted that this was the embassy of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that you were the representative of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not of the Muslim people. And my colleague asked you yesterday about the ethnic composition of the embassy, and you said -- or rather, you did not answer that question. You said that some people had Croat citizenship. I'm going to ask you quite simply. This embassy, in terms of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina itself, were there any other persons in this embassy apart from Bosniaks in view of the entire population?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In your office, was there a single person -- or rather, how many people were employed in your office? That is the most sensitive question dealing with refugees. How many people were employed in your office?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number varied between three, five, and seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was there a single Croat or Serb in your office?

utterances.speaker: AZRA KRAJSEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not look at anybody's documents. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're the only person at that point in time who did not know what somebody's ethnicity was, and you know very well that that was a moment and also today in every organ in Bosnia-Herzegovina there is proper representation of all the ethnic groups in Bosnia-Herzegovina, precisely so that some members of some ethnic groups would not consider this to be, say, a Muslim embassy. How come you cannot answer that? Thank you very much. This concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Time has come to adjourn. We'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
